key_insight: In perovskite oxides for CO2-to-CH4 conversion, the ratio of unoccupied TM 3d to occupied O 2p bandwidths (W3d/W2p) is the most useful electronic descriptor for activity, with lower values generally indicating higher CH4 activity.
engineering_relevance: This gives catalyst designers a simple, screenable electronic-structure target for prioritizing double perovskites before experimental synthesis and testing.
method: Evaluated six band-center and bandwidth descriptors for CO2-to-CH4 activity.
Used parametric brute-force searching (BFS) to fit explicit descriptor-activity equations.
Applied the selected equation to screen 24 La-based double perovskites.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports negative correlations between CH4 activity and the unoccupied TM 3d-band center, charge-transfer energy, and W3d/W2p, with screening highlighting La2CoGaO6, La2CoAlO6, and Ti-containing compositions as promising candidates.
watch_item: The descriptor-activity relationships are derived from correlations and fitted equations, so predictive value may depend on the composition range and data used for screening.
paper_title: Electronic Structure Descriptors for CO$_2$ Conversion Activity in Perovskite Oxides
